DATELINE: ITV version timestamped 17 July 2026 (Friday). The copy refers to Burnham beginning to
move into Downing Street "over the weekend", so it straddles Fri/Sat. NOT verified as a
post-10:00 Saturday 18 July development.

REPORTED CONTENT (PA):
- Burnham becomes prime minister on Monday and begins moving into Downing Street over the weekend.
- He is still "finalising" his cabinet after Westminster speculation over his choice of chancellor.
- Allies on Labour's left favour Ed Miliband; reports suggest Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood
  will get the role.
- Burnham said there had been "too much" speculation and he would announce his ministerial team
  on Monday.
- Expected to set out plans to give people "breathing space" on the cost of living.
- Core theme: devolving power from Whitehall to regions, driven from "No 10 North" in Manchester,
  which he is expected to visit during his first week in power.
- Allies said Burnham will make a "dynamic start" with measures to ease the cost-of-living squeeze.

DIRECT QUOTE ATTRIBUTED TO ANDY BURNHAM (snippet-sourced, NOT verified in approved article text):
"I am finalising those decisions, and I will come to conclusions very shortly, and then I will
announce those on Monday."

MECHANICS: Starmer visits Buckingham Palace Monday to offer his resignation to the King;
Burnham then sees the King to "kiss hands" and is invited to take over as prime minister.
